about: Rules that read differently in Vue. The lines replace the common ones; the examples are templates.

accessible-name.build: Give each icon-only button an aria-label (or a visually hidden text) taken from the translations of the project; bind dynamic attributes with a colon.
accessible-name.review: Every icon-only button in the templates has a name from the i18n messages, not a hard-coded string.

keyboard-operable.build: Use <button> and <a>, not a div with @click; bind the state of a disclosure with :aria-expanded.
keyboard-operable.review: No @click on a non-interactive element; a menu button exposes :aria-expanded.

form-labels.build: Associate each label with its input by id (use a generated id for a reusable component) and bind the error with aria-describedby.
form-labels.review: Each input in a component has a label tied by for/id, including inside reusable components.

no-double-submit.build: Disable the button while the async call runs and show a busy state; reset it in finally.
no-double-submit.review: Click the submit button twice: only one request is sent.

examples.good: <button type="submit" :disabled="submitting">Save</button>  // submitting is set before and reset in finally

loading-indicators.build: Give each view that loads data a loading, an empty and an error state, and keep the final size with a skeleton.
loading-indicators.review: Throttle the network: each view shows a placeholder, then content; a failed request shows an error state.

stable-layout.build: Give images a width, a height or an aspect ratio, and reserve a slot for late badges.
stable-layout.review: Throttle the network: the content around a late image or count does not move.
